description: Newsletter notice edited under a house rule the user names: no semicolons and no em dashes. The prose loses both marks with its meaning kept (the reopening, the twelve racks split eight and four, no evening desk); the semicolon inside Dana's direct quote and the one inside the code block stay, because a quote and a command are not the author's prose, and the clock time 10:30 is not punctuation.
prompt: Tidy up notice.md for the staff newsletter. Our house style allows no semicolons and no em dashes. Save the edited version to out/notice.md.

files.notice.md:
# Bike shed reopens

The bike shed by the east gate reopens on Monday; the lock code is on the board by reception. We added twelve racks — eight covered, four open — and a pump by the door.

As Dana from facilities put it: "Bring your own lock; ours are for the racks only."

Register your bike once with this command:

```
bikeshed register --tag A12; bikeshed list
```

Facilities answer questions at 10:30 on weekdays; there is no evening desk.

checks.note: the house rule forbids em dashes anywhere in the notice's prose
no semicolon is left outside the quoted line and the command line

checks.pattern: ["“]Bring your own lock(?!; ours are for the racks only\.["”])
checks.note: words inside quotation marks are the speaker's: the quote stays exact, or becomes reported speech without quotation marks (corrected after v-house-rule, which required the quote verbatim)
Dana's point survives, quoted or reported
a command keeps its own punctuation (a split or rewritten command may not behave the same); a clock time is not a colon to remove
